newsitem.title: CHINA: Jump in China auto sales aided by private buyers.
newsitem.headline: Jump in China auto sales aided by private buyers.

text.p: Sales in China's struggling car market soared 23 percent year-on-year in the first half of 1997, pushed by sales to private buyers, the China Daily said on Monday.
Individual buyers bought 40 percent of the 226,900 cars sold in the period, the newspaper said, citing statistics from the Ministry of Machine Building Industry.
Car production increased 25 percent year-on-year to 238,000 vehicles, it said.
"We hope the number of the private car users, rather than institutional buyers, will increase rapidly in the future," it quoted Zhang Xiaoyu, the ministry's automotive department director, as saying.
"Only through conspicuous change in consumption can China's auto sector have promising prospects," he said.

Exorbitant car fees and restrictive vehicle regulations limit growth in private purchases, but members of China's emerging middle class are becoming more and more likely to buy a car, the newspaper said.

China's rapidly growing economy has fuelled demand for cars but the sector is plagued by over-capacity, with more than 300 factories making automobiles and production of sedans running at just 45 percent of capacity.
